A new analysis of data from a large national study suggests that women with higher blood levels of two widely used industrial chemicals may face an elevated risk of an aggressive form of breast cancer. Researchers examined samples from nearly 2,000 participants and found that those in the highest quartile of exposure had roughly 1.5 times the risk of developing hormone receptor-negative tumors compared with those in the lowest quartile. The association persisted after adjustment for age, body mass index, and family history. The authors noted that the study shows an association and does not prove that the chemicals cause cancer, and that exposure was measured at a single point in time. “These findings add to the evidence that environmental exposures merit closer attention,” the lead investigator said. Further research is needed to clarify mechanisms.
